question: do transactions committed in a loop inherit the previous transaction characteristics

question: the statistics views do not show my latest activity right after running queries
answer_quote: it is important to realize that the information does not update instantaneously

question: can the replication lag times be used to predict how long the standby needs to catch up
answer_quote: The reported lag times are not predictions of how long it will take for the standby to catch up with the sending server assuming the current rate of replay.

question: can a checkpoint be skipped when nothing happened on the server
answer_quote: Checkpoints may be skipped if the server has been idle since the last one.

question: why are some combinations of backend type and object missing from the I/O statistics view
answer_quote: Some backend types never perform I/O operations on some I/O objects and/or in some I/O contexts. These rows are omitted from the view.

question: reduce the overhead from statistics collection on a busy server
answer_quote: Since collection of statistics adds some overhead to query execution, the system can be configured to collect or not collect information.

question: why do index tuples read and index tuples fetched counters differ
answer_quote: idx_tup_read counts index entries retrieved from the index while idx_tup_fetch counts live rows fetched from the table

question: how can I see which locks are currently held in the lock manager
answer_quote: It allows the database administrator to view information about the outstanding locks in the lock manager.

question: how does vacuum progress reporting handle parallel workers
answer_quote: During a parallel vacuum, the leader and each of its workers reports its own row, all sharing the same relid.

question: how do I enable DTrace probes in my build
answer_quote: By default, probes are not available, so you will need to explicitly tell the configure script to make the probes available in PostgreSQL.

question: my disk is almost full and I cannot delete anything else
answer_quote: you can move some of the database files to other file systems by making use of tablespaces

question: ANALYZE progress on a partitioned table shows the parent first
answer_quote: when ANALYZE is run on a partitioned table without the ONLY keyword, all of its partitions are also recursively analyzed

question: how should a client avoid sending a partial protocol message
answer_quote: This is commonly done by marshaling the entire message in a buffer before beginning to send it.

question: does a simple query message keep going after the first error
answer_quote: Remember that, regardless of any transaction control commands that may be present, execution of the Query message stops at the first error.

question: what does the server send when an Execute stops before finishing the portal
answer_quote: If Execute terminates before completing the execution of a portal (due to reaching a nonzero result-row count), it will send a PortalSuspended message

question: how does a client cancel a running query at the wire protocol level
answer_quote: To issue a cancel request, the frontend opens a new connection to the server and sends a CancelRequest message

question: graceful connection termination message
answer_quote: The normal, graceful termination procedure is that the frontend sends a Terminate message and immediately closes the connection.

question: how does a client begin an SSL encrypted connection at the wire protocol level
answer_quote: To initiate an SSL-encrypted connection, the frontend initially sends an SSLRequest message rather than a StartupMessage.

question: SCRAM channel binding SASL mechanism name
answer_quote: The SASL mechanism name for SCRAM with channel binding is SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS.

question: how do I start a walsender connection for physical streaming replication
answer_quote: To initiate streaming replication, the frontend sends the replication parameter in the startup message.

question: can a single WAL record be split across several WAL data messages
answer_quote: A single WAL record is never split across two WALData messages.

question: what must the slot name be when starting logical replication streaming
answer_quote: This parameter is required, and must correspond to an existing logical replication slot created with CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT in LOGICAL mode.

question: my setup script fails when it drops a table that does not exist yet
answer_quote: Attempting to drop a table that does not exist is an error.

question: what is the difference between a column default and a generated column
answer_quote: The column default is evaluated once when the row is first inserted if no other value was provided

question: my check constraint still lets NULL values through
answer_quote: a check constraint is satisfied if the check expression evaluates to true or the null value.

question: can I insert several NULLs into a column with a unique constraint
answer_quote: By default, two null values are not considered equal in this comparison.

question: keep child rows but clear the foreign key when the referenced row is deleted
answer_quote: These cause the referencing column(s) in the referencing row(s) to be set to nulls or their default values, respectively, when the referenced row is deleted.

question: can transaction IDs wrap around in a long-lived database
answer_quote: In a long-lived database it is possible for transaction IDs to wrap around.

question: temporarily turn off row level security on a table without losing my policies
answer_quote: Disabling row security does not remove any policies that are defined on the table; they are simply ignored.

question: which schema do my new tables end up in when I do not qualify the name
answer_quote: it is also the schema in which new tables will be created if the CREATE TABLE command does not specify a schema

question: permission denied for schema when selecting from another user's table
answer_quote: By default, users cannot access any objects in schemas they do not own. To allow that, the owner of the schema must grant the USAGE privilege on the schema.

question: can a table inherit from several parent tables
answer_quote: A table can inherit from more than one parent table, in which case it has the union of the columns defined by the parent tables.

question: sub-partitioning partitioned table of partitions
answer_quote: Partitions may themselves be defined as partitioned tables, resulting in sub-partitioning.

question: load data into a new partition before making it visible to queries
answer_quote: This could allow data to be loaded, checked, and transformed before being made visible to queries on the parent table.

question: round values to the nearest hundred in a numeric column
answer_quote: it is allowed to declare a numeric column with a negative scale. Then values will be rounded to the left of the decimal point.

question: what does infinity minus infinity evaluate to
answer_quote: Infinity plus any finite value equals Infinity, as does Infinity plus Infinity; but Infinity minus Infinity yields NaN

question: floating point values I stored come back slightly different
answer_quote: Inexact means that some values cannot be converted exactly to the internal format and are stored as approximations, so that storing and retrieving a value might show slight discrepancies.

question: how is a binary string different from a character string
answer_quote: A binary string is a sequence of octets (or bytes). Binary strings are distinguished from character strings in two ways.

question: my timestamp literal with a time zone is being treated as without time zone
answer_quote: PostgreSQL never examines the content of a literal string before determining its type, and therefore will treat both of the above as timestamp without time zone.

question: should I use time with time zone
answer_quote: we recommend using date/time types that contain both date and time when using time zones.

question: how are interval values stored internally
answer_quote: PostgreSQL stores interval values as months, days, and microseconds. For output, the months field is converted to years and months by dividing by 12.

question: bit string storage size overhead
answer_quote: A bit string value requires 1 byte for each group of 8 bits, plus 5 or 8 bytes overhead depending on the length of the string

question: what are lexeme weights in text search vectors used for
answer_quote: Weights are typically used to reflect document structure, for example by marking title words differently from body words.

question: XML data processing issues when encodings differ
answer_quote: processing XML data with PostgreSQL will be less error-prone and more efficient if the XML data encoding, client encoding, and server encoding are the same.

question: jsonb changed the whitespace of the document I stored
answer_quote: json outputs the same text that was input, while jsonb does not preserve semantically-insignificant details such as whitespace

question: can I test containment on json columns
answer_quote: Testing containment is an important capability of jsonb. There is no parallel set of facilities for the json type.

question: set a jsonb array element past the end of the array
answer_quote: If an index is specified for an array containing too few elements, NULL elements will be appended until the index is reachable and the value can be set.

question: how do I write a NULL element inside an array literal
answer_quote: To set an element of an array constant to NULL, write NULL for the element value.

question: connecting to a unix socket from embedded SQL fails unless the host name is right
answer_quote: Notice that when specifying a socket connection (with the unix: prefix), the host name must be exactly localhost.

question: can several threads share one connection in my embedded SQL program
answer_quote: If your application uses multiple threads of execution, they cannot share a connection concurrently.

question: when are changes committed in an embedded SQL program by default
answer_quote: In the default mode, statements are committed only when EXEC SQL COMMIT is issued.

question: the preprocessor cannot handle my struct host variable
answer_quote: The definition of a structure or union also must be listed inside a DECLARE section. Otherwise the preprocessor cannot handle these types since it does not know the definition.

question: do I need to allocate memory for interval host variables
answer_quote: It is required, however, to allocate memory for an interval type value explicitly.

question: can I use composite types as host variables in ecpg
answer_quote: Composite types are not directly supported in ECPG, but an easy workaround is possible.

question: error because a query returned multiple rows but my host variable holds only one
answer_quote: This means a query has returned multiple rows but the statement was only prepared to store one result row

question: my include file is not found by the EXEC SQL INCLUDE command
answer_quote: The include file name is case-sensitive, even though the rest of the EXEC SQL INCLUDE command follows the normal SQL case-sensitivity rules.

question: how do I compile a C program with embedded SQL statements
answer_quote: Before compiling you run the file through the embedded SQL C preprocessor

question: how can an embedded SQL application work with large objects
answer_quote: Large objects are not directly supported by ECPG, but ECPG application can manipulate large objects through the libpq large object functions

question: why does the preprocessor say a variable has no declaration inside a function
answer_quote: the ecpg preprocessor cannot find any declaration for the variable dbname in the test method, so an error will occur

question: what does the preprocessor write at the top of the generated C file
answer_quote: The first four lines written by ecpg to the output are fixed lines. Two are comments and two are include lines necessary to interface to the library.

question: ECPGdo library function
answer_quote: The most important function in the library is ECPGdo, which takes care of executing most commands.

question: what constraint applies to casts between types in a multiple-data-type operator family
answer_quote: any implicit or binary-coercion casts that are defined between data types included in the operator family must not change the associated sort ordering

question: can an operator class without a skip support function still use skip scan
answer_quote: Operator classes that do not provide a skip support function are still eligible to use skip scan.

question: how do btree indexes clean up garbage from frequent updates
answer_quote: B-Tree indexes incrementally delete version churn index tuples by performing bottom-up index deletion passes.

question: my btree index with many duplicate values takes too much space
answer_quote: Deduplication works by periodically merging groups of duplicate tuples together, forming a single posting list tuple for each group.

question: my index on an inet column is not used for network operators by default
answer_quote: For historical reasons, the inet_ops operator class is not the default class for types inet and cidr.

question: when can a GiST operator class not support index-only scans
answer_quote: If the compress method is lossy for leaf entries, the operator class cannot support index-only scans, and must not define a fetch function.

question: what does the SP-GiST core handle for an operator class developer
answer_quote: SP-GiST offers an interface with a high level of abstraction, requiring the access method developer to implement only methods specific to a given data type.

question: GIN index inserts cause occasional latency spikes, how do I get consistent response time
answer_quote: If consistent response time is more important than update speed, use of pending entries can be disabled by turning off the fastupdate storage parameter for a GIN index.

question: when does a BRIN index get summarized automatically
answer_quote: When autosummarization is enabled, a request is sent to autovacuum to execute a targeted summarization for a block range when an insertion is detected

question: what kind of workload is a hash index best at
answer_quote: Hash indexes are best optimized for SELECT and UPDATE-heavy workloads that use equality scans on larger tables.

question: are hash indexes suitable for a table that grows very quickly
answer_quote: The expansion occurs in the foreground, which could increase execution time for user inserts. Thus, hash indexes may not be suitable for tables with rapidly increasing number of rows.

question: are default values included when parsing a connection string into options
answer_quote: All legal options will be present in the result array, but the PQconninfoOption for any option not present in the connection string will have val set to NULL

question: what happens when I list several hosts in the connection string
answer_quote: When multiple hosts are specified, or when a single host name is translated to multiple addresses, all the hosts and addresses will be tried in order, until one succeeds.

question: connect without giving a host name from C
answer_quote: Without either a host name or host address, libpq will connect using a local Unix-domain socket; or on Windows, it will attempt to connect to localhost.

question: how do I turn off client TCP keepalives for a connection
answer_quote: The default value is 1, meaning on, but you can change this to 0, meaning off, if keepalives are not wanted.

question: sslcert default file location
answer_quote: This parameter specifies the file name of the client SSL certificate, replacing the default ~/.postgresql/postgresql.crt.

question: how long does a result object live after I run another command or close the connection
answer_quote: it does not go away when you issue a new command, nor even if you close the connection

question: can pipeline mode deadlock if the connection is blocking
answer_quote: If used in blocking mode it is possible for a client/server deadlock to occur.

question: when is pipeline mode not useful
answer_quote: Pipeline mode is not useful when information from one operation is required by the client to produce the next operation.

question: client encoding id not symbolic name
answer_quote: Note that it returns the encoding ID, not a symbolic string such as EUC_JP.

question: can an event procedure be registered twice on the same connection
answer_quote: A particular event procedure can be registered only once in any PGconn.

question: where do I store passwords so the client does not prompt every time
answer_quote: The file .pgpass in a user's home directory can contain passwords to be used if the connection requires a password (and no password has been specified otherwise).

question: which service definition wins when both a per-user and system service file define it
answer_quote: If the same service name exists in both the user and the system file, the user file takes precedence.

question: where do I put root certificates so the client verifies the server certificate
answer_quote: To allow server certificate verification, one or more root certificates must be placed in the file ~/.postgresql/root.crt in the user's home directory.

question: what is the difference between verify-ca and verify-full
answer_quote: The difference between verify-ca and verify-full depends on the policy of the root CA.

question: can several threads issue commands over one connection object
answer_quote: As of version 17, libpq is always reentrant and thread-safe. However, one restriction is that no two threads attempt to manipulate the same PGconn object at the same time.

question: how are combinations of polymorphic argument types restricted when several arguments use them
answer_quote: when more than one argument position is declared with a polymorphic type, the net effect is that only certain combinations of actual argument types are allowed

question: what does an INOUT parameter mean in a function declaration
answer_quote: An INOUT parameter serves as both an input parameter (part of the calling argument list) and an output parameter (part of the result record type).

question: how can I pass an array directly to a variadic function
answer_quote: This prevents expansion of the function's variadic parameter into its element type, thereby allowing the array argument value to match normally.

question: my polymorphic function fails when I pass an integer and a float together
answer_quote: you must provide two arguments that are of exactly the same data type; the system will not attempt to resolve any type differences

question: can a function that only does SELECT be marked STABLE even when other transactions modify the tables
answer_quote: a function containing only SELECT commands can safely be marked STABLE, even if it selects from tables that might be undergoing modifications by concurrent queries

question: how do I set the length header of a variable-length C type
answer_quote: All variable-length types must begin with an opaque length field of exactly 4 bytes, which will be set by SET_VARSIZE

question: named SQL function arguments since version
answer_quote: The ability to use names to reference SQL function arguments was added in PostgreSQL 9.2.

question: tell the planner my function is expensive and its cost depends on inputs
answer_quote: If the target function's run time is highly dependent on its inputs, it may be useful to provide a non-constant cost estimate for it.

question: my custom aggregate with an internal state cannot run in parallel
answer_quote: When the aggregate's state type is declared as internal, it is usually also appropriate for the aggregate definition to provide a serialization function and a deserialization function

question: what functions must a user-defined base type provide
answer_quote: A user-defined type must always have input and output functions.

question: what does it mean for one operator to be the commutator of another
answer_quote: We say that operator A is the commutator of operator B if (x A y) equals (y B x) for all possible input values x, y.

question: how do I allow my custom operator to be used by merge joins
answer_quote: The MERGES clause, if present, tells the system that it is permissible to use the merge-join method for a join based on this operator.

question: what return type must index search operators have
answer_quote: all operators defined as index method search operators must return type boolean

question: my extension script has CREATE POLICY statements and fails
answer_quote: PostgreSQL does not currently support extension scripts issuing CREATE POLICY or SECURITY LABEL statements.

question: how does an index method know about the data types it works with
answer_quote: The routines for an index method do not directly know anything about the data types that the index method will operate on.

question: change the port the server listens on
answer_quote: The TCP port the server listens on; 5432 by default. Note that the same port number is used for all IP addresses the server listens on.

question: provide the SSL private key passphrase without a prompt at startup
answer_quote: The command does not actually have to prompt the user for a passphrase. It can read it from a file, obtain it from a keychain facility, or similar.

question: maximum time between automatic WAL checkpoints
answer_quote: The valid range is between 30 seconds and one day. The default is five minutes (5min).

question: keep enough WAL around for a standby that falls behind
answer_quote: Specifies the minimum size of past WAL files kept in the pg_wal directory, in case a standby server needs to fetch them for streaming replication.

question: why does a delayed standby use more disk space
answer_quote: Therefore, longer delays will result in a greater accumulation of WAL files, increasing disk space requirements for the standby's pg_wal directory.

question: discourage sequential scans to test whether an index plan is better
answer_quote: It is impossible to suppress sequential scans entirely, but turning this variable off discourages the planner from using one if there are other methods

question: planner assumed disk cache size
answer_quote: Sets the planner's assumption about the effective size of the disk cache that is available to a single query.

question: my server log lines run into the message text and are hard to read
answer_quote: you should usually make its last character be a space, to provide visual separation from the rest of the log line

question: why is a statement with a syntax error missing from the statement log
answer_quote: Statements that contain simple syntax errors are not logged even by the log_statement = all setting, because the log message is emitted only after basic parsing

question: is the process title updated on Windows by default
answer_quote: This setting defaults to on on most platforms, but it defaults to off on Windows due to that platform's larger overhead for updating

question: how does the autovacuum scale factor relate to table size
answer_quote: Specifies a fraction of the table size to add to autovacuum_vacuum_threshold when deciding whether to trigger a VACUUM. The default is 0.2 (20% of table size).

question: row_security error instead of applying policy
answer_quote: This variable controls whether to raise an error in lieu of applying a row security policy.

question: how is statement timeout measured
answer_quote: The timeout is measured from the time a command arrives at the server until it is completed by the server.

question: which libraries must be preloaded at server start
answer_quote: Some libraries need to perform certain operations that can only take place at postmaster start, such as allocating shared memory, reserving light-weight locks, or starting background workers.

question: does statement sampling override the minimum duration logging
answer_quote: This setting has lower priority than log_min_duration_statement, meaning that statements with durations exceeding log_min_duration_statement are not subject to sampling and are always logged.

question: attributes view composite data types
answer_quote: The view attributes contains information about the attributes of composite data types defined in the database.

question: what data types do information schema columns use
answer_quote: These are defined as simple domains over ordinary built-in types.

question: list all columns of all tables and views in the database
answer_quote: The view columns contains information about all table columns (or view columns) in the database. System columns (ctid, etc.) are not included.

question: constraint_table_usage view
answer_quote: The view constraint_table_usage identifies all tables in the current database that are used by some constraint and are owned by a currently enabled role.

question: which tables does a function or procedure use
answer_quote: The view routine_table_usage is meant to identify all tables that are used by a function or procedure. This information is currently not tracked by PostgreSQL.

question: sql_sizing size limits table
answer_quote: The table sql_sizing contains information about various size limits and maximum values in PostgreSQL.

question: why do sequence SELECT and UPDATE privileges not show in the information schema
answer_quote: In PostgreSQL, sequences also support SELECT and UPDATE privileges in addition to the USAGE privilege. These are nonstandard and therefore not visible in the information schema.

question: which routines does a view depend on
answer_quote: The view view_routine_usage identifies all routines (functions and procedures) that are used in the query expression of a view
